top5_argument: This is the shortlist's named test. My analysis says it can only run on PSL_2(Z)-Farey cells. For A != Z, PSL_2(A) contains dilations fixing every cell, so the projective renormalisation is not unique and (T_I)_J = T_{I.J} fails. The rerun therefore reproves Thurston's projective copy of F and still needs the overgroup lemma; it cannot avoid embedding F. It remains worth running as an affine-to-projective portability test, and it would remove Carriere-Ghys from Monod's theorem. The statement takes under 300 lines (piecewise-Mobius carrier). There is no formal baseline.
title: Monod's H(A) nonamenable, by rerunning the device on Farey (projective) cells
statement: For a subring A of R, the group H(A) of piecewise-PSL_2(A) homeomorphisms of the projective line (breakpoints in the fixed-point set P_A) is nonamenable. The new case is A = Z; A != Z is Monod 2013.
reference: Monod, PNAS 110 (2013) 4524-4527; Monod arXiv:2305.00796; Thurston (H_Q(Z) is isomorphic to F).
status: A != Z: known (Monod, via Carriere-Ghys). A = Z: follows from 248 via Thurston's isomorphism.
how_item_helps: SKEPTICAL FINDING. The rerun works only on PSL_2(Z)-Farey cells. For A != Z the stabiliser in PSL_2(A) of a cell contains hyperbolic dilations x -> lambda^2 x (lambda a unit of A, e.g. 2 for Z[1/2]). So the projective renormalisation T_I is not unique, condition (a) (T_I)_J = T_{I.J} fails, and covariance under general g in H(A) is lost. The rerun therefore reproves nonamenability of Thurston's copy of F (projective model) and then needs the overgroup lemma. It is still a useful portability test, because the renormalisation changes from affine to projective. It does not remove the embedding of F; it only replaces the Minkowski-?-conjugation by a native projective run.
expected: low-med (removes Carriere-Ghys for every A, but only through the F copy)
confidence: medium (that it works on PSL_2(Z) cells); high (that it cannot run natively on PSL_2(A) cells for A != Z)

title: Depth-3 parity lower bound 2^{Omega(sqrt n)} (Håstad 1986/89; PPZ99 sharp form)
statement: Every OR-AND-OR circuit computing parity of n bits has 2^{c·sqrt n} gates for some absolute c > 0 (sharp: Theta(n^{1/4} 2^{sqrt n}), PPZ99).
reference: J. Håstad, 'Almost optimal lower bounds for small depth circuits', STOC 1986 / Computational limitations of small-depth circuits (MIT Press 1987), cited as H89; Paturi-Pudlák-Zane, 'Satisfiability coding lemma', Chicago J. TCS 1999, Thm 6; HJP95 Thm 3.3.
how_item_helps: With C1 and the f-generic Lean skeleton (wide_correlation_of_good_restrictions plus a re-parametrised circuit_lower_bound_of_small_cnf_correlations), the only new ingredient is a parity-vs-narrow-CNF correlation bound corr_b(parity on m live vars) <= 2^{-Omega(m/b)}. That bound is expected true but was NOT verified here, and the paper does not state it. Taking b = O(1) and pk a small constant gives 2^{c sqrt n}. This replaces the switching lemma by C1. It would not beat the short PPZ argument, so the gain is mainly against the switching-lemma route.

statement: Every polylog(m/epsilon)-wise independent distribution epsilon-fools every m-clause CNF.

But Bazzi's bound depends on m only polylogarithmically, and fooling needs the distribution itself, not a random restriction, so the fit is weak.

title: N1 (proved-false analogue): latent gadget with p_* = 0
statement: There is no Data g over K = F_2^l with stabilityError g = 0 and kernelError <= nu < 1 for every S of restriction rank >= r, whenever l >= r.
how_item_helps: If C(x+a) = C(x) for all a in supp(mu), let A = span(supp mu). Equivariance forces A ∩ K = 0. Then G = A^perp restricts onto all of K^*, so it has rank l >= r_*, yet it vanishes on every noise vector, so the detection probability is 0. Any gadget must therefore pay p > 0. This is why perfect-completeness results (105, approximate coloring under 2-to-1) cannot use it as completeness noise.

top5_argument: The bridge's output (exists_effective_critical_bound with the selector projection) is exactly the input Ten Advances' Stage 2 asks for, at growing degree. A prover with the 108 library should replace the about 8k-line minor-sum critical-locus block and reach Theta(n^2 log n). Guo v2 did this on paper within days. There is a formal baseline to compare against (ten-proofs Permanent.lean), and stating it needs only a ported circuit model. Caveat: same polynomial, different measure. This is evidence of device reuse but not cross-problem generality.
title: Ten Advances Ch. 5: circuit lower bound for the permanent (and its n^2 log n strengthening)
statement: Division-free arithmetic circuits computing per_n over C need Omega(n^2 log log n) gates (Ten Advances). Strengthening via the bridge (Guo v2): L_div(per_n) >= (n^2/119790) log2(n/44) for n >= 1936.
reference: OpenAI, 'Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science' (1 Aug 2026), Ch. 5 'Circuit and Formula Lower Bounds for the Permanent', https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/ten-proofs-oai.pdf; Lean: github.com/openai/ten-proofs Permanent.lean; J. Guo, arXiv:2609.29568v2 (8 Oct 2026).
status: n^2 log log n: known (model-produced, Lean-certified). n^2 log n: Guo v2, written deduction from 12 machine-checked 108 declarations, not formalized end to end.
how_item_helps: Ten Advances Stage 2 needs a degree-d permanent specialization with critical codimension k = Theta(n^2). Its Stage 3 gets that only at bounded degree, via minor sums M_{t,s,d}, power sums and Möbius inclusion-exclusion; the chapter names 'd growing with n' as the next target. The bridge's output exists_effective_critical_bound plus exists_selector_affine_projection gives degree about k/3 with codimension >= floor(C(q+2,2)/18). Feeding it into the slicing lemma (exists_slicedGradient_of_criticalLocus_codimension in ten-proofs) and the Bezout/Baur-Strassen count gives k log(d-1)/3 = Theta(n^2 log n). This replaces the about 8k-line minor-sum block and strengthens the bound.

title: Replace CAT(0) by injective metric spaces / Helly graphs (spaces with convex geodesic bicombings)
how_item_helps: Every hyperbolic group acts geometrically on a proper injective metric space (Lang 2013) and is Helly (Chalopin–Chepoi–Genevois–Hirai–Osajda) [memory]. The conditional test breaks there because tangent cones have no inner-product pairing and inductive means lack Sturm's variance bound. A prover that 'proves' no-action for injective targets has a bug.

statement: Run random triangle removal from K_n to density p = n^{-1/2+eps}. title: Kalton's question for proper / bounded-geometry uniformly discrete spaces
statement: Does F(M) have the BAP for every uniformly discrete M that is proper (closed balls finite), e.g. every locally finite graph of bounded degree, or every finitely generated group with a word metric?
reference: Kalton, Collect. Math. 55 (2004) 171–217, p. 185 (general question); Godefroy survey, Comment. Math. 55(2) (2015) 89–118, Problem 6.2, https://bibliotekanauki.pl/articles/746348.pdf; Hájek–Medina, arXiv 2112.03095, https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03095 (reduction to nets; Schauder bases for nets in some spaces) [subagent-verified]. I found no explicit listing of the proper/bounded-geometry special case.
status: not found as a listed problem. 330 answers the general question with a non-proper space (the Lean proves `¬ ProperSpace M`), so the proper case becomes the natural residual question [status unverified].
how_item_helps: Direct transfer fails. The anchors attach infinitely many vertices at distance R, so each block is bounded but not proper. In a proper space a bounded block is finite, and then F is finite-dimensional with 1-BAP. Adaptation: replace one anchor per label by a finite hub tree of depth ~log, and let blocks be unbounded but uniformly locally finite. The averaging is already independent of |S|, but `bump_mass` uses d(x, a(x)) ≤ R with a fixed finite anchor set, so the 3L/4 bump bound breaks once anchors move to distance ~log|G|. This is a genuine obstacle. If it can be overcome, the payoff is large.

reference: Bourgain 1989 (IHES) Lemma 4.11; Nazarov-Oberlin-Thiele arXiv:0912.3010; Krause-Mirek-Trojan arXiv:1504.04132; Krause arXiv:2502.12887
status: the Euclidean smooth-window version is known with (log N)^2, and the optimal power is open. For this rough dyadic-average variant I have NOT verified that the same bound is in the literature; check before use.

title: Garcia-Fritz-Pasten-Vidaux: positive-existential interpretation of (N,+,x) in Q with height-comparison predicates

how_item_helps: C1 on CW_q is a degeneration from CW_q^{tensor n} times a group tensor; over C the group tensor is a unit tensor after Fourier, so the irreversibility/universal-method barrier still applies (M2's 2.290 and 2.258 respect it). A prover success here would indicate a library or barrier-scope error. M1 escapes only by switching to C(a,b), whose irreversibility tends to 1.

title: Patterson's first moment of cubic Gauss sums over primary Eisenstein primes (release family 023, formalized)
statement: sum over primary Eisenstein primes p with N p <= X of g~(p) = (6/5) c_* X^{5/6}/log X + o(X^{5/6}/log X), c_* = (2 pi)^{2/3}/(3 Gamma(2/3)); plus angular comparison and cancellation in every nonzero angular mode.
reference: Patterson 1978 (conjecture); Heath-Brown-Patterson 1979; Heath-Brown 2000; Dunn-Radziwill, Ann. of Math. 200 (2024), conditional on GRH; release family 023 'An unconditional first moment for cubic Gauss sums' (2026-09-25), unconditional, with Lean.
status: proved conditionally (DR 2024) and, per the release, unconditionally (023, Lean comparator PattersonFirstMoment; result of a comparator run not recorded in data/lean_checks.json).
how_item_helps: 023 handles the prime sum with classical zero-free regions plus Type I/II bounds. The device supplies exactly the Mobius-weighted (Type I with mu) cubic/sextic Gauss-sum averages with square-root cancellation on average (RawMoment), and the local identity breveGamma1_gamma2_eq_neg_alpha_G links sextic Gauss sums at primes to Hecke characters. A prover with the device should need far less of 023's dispersion machinery. The third arm (7/8 Hecke theorem available) tests theorem-level reuse: a zero-free half-plane for cubic Hecke L-functions is the kind of input DR needed GRH for.

reference: Heath-Brown, Quart. J. Math. Oxford (2) 37 (1986) 27-38 (search summary); release family 029 claims every admissible base by a route that reuses the device.
how_item_helps: 029's route: a common zero-free strip for Hecke L-functions over cyclotomic F containing mu_12 (built with sextic Kummer twists and cubic theta, i.e. the device ported from Q(sqrt-3) to F) gives a power-saving count of primes splitting in Kummer fields, which removes index divisors. With the device in L, a prover could aim at the strictly stronger single-base statement; the sieve route is the comparison arm.
confidence: low (porting the device to cyclotomic F needs Kazhdan-Patterson theta over F, which OAI does not have)

current_proof_size: about 12 pages on top of Chen / Fouvry-Iwaniec sieve input. No formalization known.

title: Hyperinvariant subspace problem on reflexive non-Hilbert spaces: L^p[0,1] (1<p<inf, p != 2)
statement: Does every nonscalar bounded operator on L^p[0,1] (equivalently on L^p(Z_2; l^p(Z)), an isomorphic copy) have a nontrivial closed hyperinvariant subspace? Target: a nonzero norm-quasinilpotent operator on L^p(Z_2, Haar; l^p(Z)) whose commutant has no nontrivial closed common invariant subspace.
reference: Search snippet (JOT 73:1 (2015), theta.ro): 'the invariant and hyperinvariant subspace problem are still open in reflexive Banach spaces, and in particular in Hilbert spaces'; Read/Enflo counterexamples are on non-reflexive spaces (l^1, c_0); Argyros-Haydon space gives a positive HSP. Domar 1981 (Math. Scand. 49) is the classical weighted-translation source BI follows (whether it covers l^p for p != 2 was not verified here).
status: open as of the search snippets (HSP on reflexive spaces other than Hilbert); BI settles only p = 2.
how_item_helps: (1) Fiber criterion on weighted l^p(Z): redo SupportSeparation / quadratic_fiber_tails with dual sequences c in l^q (SupportSeparation already has the dual-pairing shape (sum b_j c_{j-r}) with ||c_j|| w_j <= 1). (2) Global: replace L.orthogonal by a nonzero functional vanishing on L (Hahn-Banach, Mathlib exists_dual_vector / separating dual) and represent it fiberwise as z in L^q(X; l^q) (needs vector-valued L^p duality, not in Mathlib). (3) E1 and the descent (ergodic_late_intersection) unchanged. Note L^p(X; l^p) ~ L^p[0,1] (non-atomic), not l^p; an l^p version would need an atomic base, where the descent fails (see N3).
expected: high (first HSP counterexample on a reflexive non-Hilbert space, if the fiber criterion holds on l^p)
lean_statable_with: Mathlib: lp with Fact (1 ≤ p), MeasureTheory.Lp, ContinuousLinearMap, Submodule, IsClosed; OAI: baseMeasure from BackwardIntertwiners/HaarBase.lean (or restate the Haar base; 30 lines). Do not include AlgebraCorollary/OperatorTransport (they contain the theorem). E1-specific budget removed: ~430 lines of definitions/lemmas + ~70 lines of use. For this target also give the p-generic fiberWeightedPermutation (FiberMaps) in both arms.

title: HSP witness fibred over an irrational rotation (Rokhlin towers replace odometer residues)

Stronger (needs the Rokhlin lemma): the same over every ergodic aperiodic invertible probability-preserving system.

title: Plumbing control: bounded backward-type intertwiners between two bilateral weighted shifts (Shields-type criterion)
statement: Let S_beta, S_gamma be injective bilateral weighted shifts on l^2(Z) with positive bounded weights. There is a nonzero bounded X with S_gamma X = X S_beta and X e_j in C e_{j-1} for all j iff the sequence r defined by r_0 = 1, r_{j+1} = r_j * gamma_{j-1}/beta_j (j in Z) is bounded; then X = (r_j / sup r) e_j -> e_{j-1} up to scale.
reference: Shields, 'Weighted shift operators and analytic function theory' (Math Surveys 13, 1974) - intertwiners/similarity of weighted shifts (from memory; statement here is mine). BI Lemma 4.2 is the fibred instance with gamma = beta(theta x).
how_item_helps: Uses only the generic half of E1 (rawBackward_recurrence pattern, sup normalization backwardBound/backwardCoeff, fiberWeightedPermutation norm bound) and NOT the opposite-drift design. Run it as a CONTROL: if the 'with item' arm gives a large speedup here, that speedup is plumbing, and the same share should be discounted from S1/S2/O1 speedups.

title: N3. Finite base / finite multiplicity (and Lomonosov): device must fail
statement: Over a finite cycle base Z/N (operator-weighted shift of multiplicity N) with fibers satisfying QuadraticWeights, there is no V with V_i e_j = b_i(j) e_{j-1} into fiber i+1, all b_i(j) > 0, 0 <= b <= 1, commuting with S: V^N restricted to a fiber is a backward shift by N in {S_x}', which grows like exp(2cNj) and must vanish. Consistent with Lomonosov: over a finite base S is compact (each fiber is compact, BI forwardFiber_compact), so S has a hyperinvariant subspace. Atomic infinite base (Z, translation): Poincare recurrence fails and the descent field s(n) = h - n is consistent; in BI's own Lean the integer orbit is exactly what goodBase removes.
how_item_helps: Proved-false analogue: Lomonosov's theorem (any T commuting with a nonzero compact has a hyperinvariant subspace) forbids the conclusion over finite bases, and the explicit cycle argument shows the device step itself (bounded positive V) is what breaks. Note: the recurrence form must be checked against forwardFiber_weight_coordinates when formalizing (beta_j = w_{j+1}/w_j in BI's convention).

title: Odd distances: every finite colouring of the plane has a monochromatic pair at odd integer distance (Davies)
statement: For every k and every c : R^2 -> [k] there are x, y with c(x) = c(y) and |x-y| an odd integer.
reference: J. Davies, "Odd distances in colourings of the plane", arXiv:2209.15598 (resolves a conjecture of Soifer; proof described as a spectral method).
status: known theorem (2022); no Lean formalization found
how_item_helps: Device route: assume a k-colouring with no monochromatic odd distance. The odd integers are in F (real algebraic), so the distance-set version of the transfer (C1 + C2) gives a measurable weak k-colouring whose classes have zero pair-correlation at every odd radius. The densest class has positive upper density, so weak FKW gives positive correlation at all radii >= d0, a contradiction. The geometric/spectral finite-graph work in Davies' proof is replaced by C1 (wild laws are Haar) plus a classical measurable density theorem. This is device reuse: it is NOT a corollary of chi >= 6.
expected: high (if the distance-set transfer holds; see N2)
confidence: medium (two inferences unverified from sources: the a.e. pair-correlation form of Bourgain/FKW, and that nothing in C1/C2 uses distance 1 beyond Proper)

Math. 2024/25 (finite-dim classes only); Hyers-Ulam / Omladič-Šemrl 1995 (whole spaces, 2ε sharp); Matoušková, 'Almost isometries of balls', JFA 190 (2002) 507-525 (bi-Lipschitz near-isometries of Euclidean balls far from isometries: a warning that the multiplicative version fails). title: S1. Finite-dimensional stability of sphere isometries (Vestfrid): ε-isometries of the unit spheres of ℓ2^n, ℓ∞^n and ℓ1^n are uniformly close to linear isometries
statement: If f : S_X → S_X (X = ℓ2^n, ℓ∞^n or ℓ1^n) is a surjective ε-isometry, |‖f(x)-f(y)‖-‖x-y‖| ≤ ε, then there is a linear isometry T with sup_{x∈S_X} ‖f(x)-Tx‖ ≤ C(n)·ε (exact constants not verified).
reference: I. A. Vestfrid, 'Near-isometries of the unit sphere', Ukrainian Math. J. 72(4) (2020) (ℓ2^n, ℓ∞^n); I. A. Vestfrid, 'ε-isometries of the unit sphere in ℓ1^n', Colloq. Math. 177 (2024) 127-133, DOI 10.4064/cm9491-1-2025. Abstracts only (search summaries); full texts not read.
how_item_helps: The device turns an attained extremal defect into an exact fixed-point configuration. With ε-slack, extremality gives r ≥ u + M - ε and s = p + M on E, so the two-point estimate becomes γ·dist + scalar oscillation + O(ε) with γ = (1-M/(1+t))^2. A χ-contraction with additive error gives an invariant convex set of χ ≤ O(ε)/(1-γ) = O(ε/M), i.e. approximately aligned chords; a quantitative chord contradiction would then bound M ≤ C√ε (or Cε^α) uniformly in n. This would replace three class-specific arguments by one dimension-free argument. The final step (approximately radial T ⇒ near a linear isometry) is NOT supplied by the device and is a real gap (Omladič-Šemrl/Hyers-Ulam need a uniform global ε-isometry; T is only ε·‖x‖-close).
expected: low-med (paper level: a uniform proof is plausible but the rate may be worse than Vestfrid's; Lean: the existing lemmas are stated for exact isometries f : UnitSphere X ≃ᵢ UnitSphere Y and must be re-proved with slack)

title: S2. Darbo applications for maps that are Lipschitz up to the oscillation of finitely many bounded scalar observables (generic shell, calibration target)
statement: If g maps a nonempty closed bounded convex C in a Banach space continuously into itself, and dist(g v, g v') ≤ γ dist(v,v') + K Σ_i |φ_i(v) - φ_i(v')| for finitely many bounded φ_i : C → ℝ and γ < 1, then g has a fixed point (because χ(gH) ≤ γ χ(H)). Instances: existence theorems for nonlinear functional-integral equations proved by Darbo in the Banaś-Goebel tradition where the nonlinearity enters through finitely many scalar functionals.
reference: Darbo 1955; Sadovskii 1967; J. Banaś, K. Goebel, Measures of Noncompactness in Banach Spaces (1980). The scalar-binning lemma is OAI.Tingley.finiteDiameterCover_image_of_scalar_bins (ReturnMapNoncompactness.lean:21).
how_item_helps: exists_fixedPoint_of_return_estimate / chi_return_image_le are map-agnostic: any g with that two-point estimate gets a fixed point with zero additional analysis. title: O1. Henry's pushout conjecture / homotopy hypothesis for Grothendieck coherators OUTSIDE the Ara-Henry arity convention
statement: Let C be a Grothendieck coherator in Maltsiniotis' general sense, where generating fillers d_j -> S may have dim(S) > j. Is every pushout of J_n along a cell of a cellular C-model a weak equivalence? Equivalently, does the homotopy hypothesis hold for all coherators, so that the theory is independent of the coherator?
reference: Maltsiniotis 2010 (arXiv:1009.2331); Ara 2013 (arXiv:1206.2941) Secs 2.3, 2.9-2.11; Henry 2016 Sec 5.3; 312 Def 1.1 and 02-cutoffs-trees.tex:40-66
status: open. 312 restricts to the convention; no source found resolving the general case (snippet-level).
how_item_helps: (a) Replace R_q by a cutoff in which operations with high-arity inputs are interpreted on unique fillers. This needs the high cells to be determined, so try a two-parameter cutoff (q, q') with q' >= max arity height of the generators needed below q. That bound is finite at each tower stage, but not uniformly. (b) Alternatively, prove that every coherator receives a convention coherator by an equivalence on models that preserves J-pushouts, then transport. (c) Run the existing ExpansionContraction/cylinderPathData chain unchanged on top of the new cutoff. This is a clean device-reuse test, because only the reflector changes.

title: S2. Model structure on algebraic Kan complexes (pushouts of free filler attachments are weak equivalences)
statement: Algebraic Kan complexes (simplicial sets with chosen horn fillers, i.e. algebras for the free-filler monad) carry a combinatorial model structure Quillen equivalent to sSet; in particular the unit X -> free algebraic Kan complex on X, and pushouts of free horn-filler attachments, are weak equivalences.
reference: Nikolaus, 'Algebraic models for higher categories', Indag. Math. 21 (2011) 52-75, arXiv:1003.1342
how_item_helps: This is the same obstruction in simplicial form: freely adjoining fillers creates new composites and must not change the homotopy type. The device's analogue would be a cutoff at a coskeletal level q (Mathlib has Coskeletal), with descending induction on the horn dimension, where partial Delta^1-cylinders that are stationary below n get their fillers from higher horn dimensions. Nikolaus avoids the problem by transfer, because the underlying simplicial sets are already fibrant and the free functor preserves anodyne maps. The device is therefore unnecessary and probably longer.

statement: Every (K,C)-quasi-isometry of DL(m,n) is at bounded distance B(K,C) from a height-respecting map (height-preserving, or height-reversing when m=n); hence F wr Z and F' wr Z are QI iff |F|,|F'| are powers of a common integer.
reference: Eskin-Fisher-Whyte, Coarse differentiation of quasi-isometries I (Annals 176, 2012) and II: Rigidity for Sol and lamplighter groups (Annals 177, 2013), arXiv math/0511647, 0706.0940
how_item_helps: For m=n the only nontrivial label is the flip A=-1, i.e. the reflection at the endpoint facet of the height interval. If adjacent tiles of the coarse-differentiation tiling carried opposite labels, C1's alternating bundles (one step on each sheet, tree box volumes exact powers of n) give a target terminal count n^{2r|E|} against a source count n^{r|E|}. This would replace EFW's orientation-consistency step. It does NOT replace coarse differentiation or the quadrilateral argument that makes each tile height-respecting, which is the bulk of EFW.

statement: If G, G' are connected simply connected real-triangulable unimodular Lie groups and F : G -> G' is a (K,C)-QI, then there is a linear L : W -> W' with P_{G'} o L = P_G (so p' o L = p and L conjugates A_G to A_{G'}) and ||pi'F(g) - pi'F(1) - L pi(g)|| <= B(G,G',K,C).

Peng I treats QIs between two groups of her class locally (search snippet, arXiv 0802.2596).

title: Local pure-type estimate with non-uniform depths (local Herzog-Kuhl / HHS lower bound)
statement: Same setting as Thm 2.1 but the i-th differential has entries in I^{s_i} (s_i >= 1 not all equal). Put d_i = s_1+...+s_i. Is lambda H_0(F) >= mu b_0 prod_{i=1}^h d_i / h! * (1 - o(1)) as min s_i -> infinity, uniformly in C, lambda, F? For s_i = s this is exactly Thm 2.1 (prod(is)/h! = s^h). The graded analogue for pure resolutions is the Herzog-Kuhl / Huneke-Miller formula l(M) = b_0 prod d_i / h!, and its non-pure form is the HHS lower bound proved by Eisenbud-Schreyer.
reference: Posed here as a device test. Background: Eisenbud-Schreyer, JAMS 22 (2009) (HHS lower bound via pairing); Herzog-Kuhl 1984; Herzog-Srinivasan, Trans. AMS 350 (1998) (multiplicity conjecture); BEKS, 'Shapes of free resolutions over a local ring', Math. Ann. (2012), arXiv:1105.2244
status: open as far as found: searches for a local HHS-type bound in terms of m-adic depth of the differentials returned only graded results (snippet level; UNVERIFIED)

title: IMW 2022: Dutta multiplicity >= e(R) for localized standard graded algebras in char p

reference: Iyengar-Ma-Walker, 'Multiplicities and Betti numbers in local algebra via lim Ulrich points', Algebra Number Theory 16 (2022) 1213-1257, arXiv:2104.10140 (main Dutta-multiplicity theorem; exact theorem number unverified, abstract read via search snippet only)
status: known (proved via lim Ulrich sequences built from sheaves on Proj)
how_item_helps: Completion is a flat local map with mS = n, preserving dimension, e and chi_infty (DuttaBaseChange.lean / multiplicity_eq_of_map_maximalIdeal already do this for residue extensions). Then dutta_complete_charp (no domain hypothesis) gives the bound. With the item in L the proof is glue (completion is complete Noetherian local of char p); without it there is no short route (the lim-Ulrich proof is long and uses graded geometry absent from Mathlib).

title: Lins-de Melo-Pugh bound for degree <= 4: at most ONE limit cycle (Li-Llibre 2012 for n=4; LMP 1977 for n=3)
statement: For every real polynomial F with deg F <= 4, x'=y-F(x), y'=-x has at most one limit cycle. (Li-Llibre also prove hyperbolicity; not part of this target.)
reference: C. Li, J. Llibre, Uniqueness of limit cycles for Lienard differential equations of degree four, J. Differential Equations 252 (2012) 3142-3162 (21 pp); A. Lins, W. de Melo, C. Pugh, On Lienard's equation, LNM 597 (1977) for n=3.
how_item_helps: NOT a corollary of Theorem 1.1 (which gives only <=2 for deg<=4), but falls out of the family's own case lemmas in a few lines. With a5=0 the reflection F->-F (limitCycle_encard_neg) lets one assume a3>=0 instead of a5>=0, which removes case 2 entirely: a1>=0 gives case 1 (no periodic orbit, or the even/centre case with no isolated zeros), a1<0 gives case 3, where matching_zeros_case3 already bounds ALL zeros of the matching function by 1. Case 3 uses E1 decisively: axisKappa is fitK of the axis data, kappa_range_height/axisKappa_lower bound the fitted curvature by the actual curvature (curvature comparison), and matchingDelta_zero_bound converts kappa_+ > kappa_- at zeros into Delta'>0 via v_kappa = G/P > 0. The proof does NOT use fit_transport or the model inequality (E2): transitive closure of {matching_zeros_case3, no_periodic_case1, limitCycle_encard_le_matching, limitCycle_encard_neg, no_isolated_matching_even} = 827 decls / 7,746 DAG lines (65% of main's 11,947), of which 165 decls / 1,438 lines depend on H; model_inequality and fit_transport are outside it. 143b does not mention that it re-proves Li-Llibre.

title: Zhang Zhifen uniqueness theorem, restoring force g(x)=x
statement: If F is smooth (polynomial for the Lean version), F(0)=0, and F'(x)/x is nondecreasing on (0,inf) and on (-inf,0) (not constant near 0), then x'=y-F(x), y'=-x has at most one limit cycle (hyperbolic if it exists).
reference: Zhang Zhifen, Acta Math. Sinica 1958 (Chinese); Zhang Zhifen et al., Qualitative Theory of Differential Equations, AMS Transl. Math. Monographs 101 (1992), Ch. 4; Coppel 1989 survey. Exact theorem numbers unverified (search snippet / domain knowledge; full text not read: arxiv.org and ddd.uab.cat unreachable).
how_item_helps: In Filippov coordinates u=x^2/2, phi_+'(u)=F'(x)/x for x>0 and phi_-'(u)=F'(x)/x for x<0 (u decreasing in x), so the hypothesis is exactly phi_+''>=0>=phi_-''. The fitted-curvature range lemma then gives kappa_+(0,r) > kappa_-(0,r) and matchingDelta_zero_bound gives Delta'>0 at every zero: <=1 cycle. This is the paper's case-3 template with the coefficient sign test replaced by the Zhang hypothesis. Needs a strict separation at the axis (paper used delta>0 from p''->inf); with only weak monotonicity a nonconstancy argument is needed.

title: NC1 (proved-false analogue): Q3 = Levi graph of the tetrahedron boundary
